# WO-605: One keychain entry shared by every data folder; wiping a test folder destroys the real key
Status: queued (in-house, contract)
Vendor: claude
Agent: orchestrator
Owner: orchestrator (contract)
Owner contact: Morgan Reyes
Kind: security
Tier: deep
Severity: HIGH (data loss)
Target release: 0.3.x hotfix
Source: owner real-data test, stage 1 (search only), qa-security 2026-11-11. Private results are kept outside the repo; this WO is PII-free by rule.

## Goal
`crypto.SERVICE`/`crypto.KEY_NAME` ("freemyid"/"db-key-v1", `crypto.py:29-30`) name ONE keychain entry for every `FREEMYID_HOME`. The SEC-72 guard (`secret_backends.py:24-32`, `_keychain_key_is_ours` at `:706-717`, `wipe_data_keys` at `:720-737`) only protects folders that hold a *different* key. But a new keyring-backed folder never gets a different key: `_keyring_get_or_create_key` (`crypto.py:99-113`) reads the existing entry first and silently adopts it. Sequence: the real folder uses key K1 -> a test/second folder starts and adopts K1 -> its DB key_check is made with K1 -> `freemyid wipe` on the test folder proves "ours" and deletes K1 -> the next start creates K2 -> the real folder now fails with "encryption key does not match this database" and K1 is gone. A real data folder on the owner's machine now reports that mismatch, most likely by this path (not repaired; code analysis only). This is the "Residual" the module doc accepts; it is not acceptable for a product whose users will run a second folder (family members, tests, support).

## Acceptance criteria (testable)
1. A new data folder never adopts an existing keychain key: non-default homes use a per-folder entry name (e.g. `db-key-v1:<sha256(resolved home)[:16]>`); the legacy `db-key-v1` stays only for the default home and is never moved silently (Windows constraint in the module doc).
2. `wipe` deletes only the entry named for this folder. The legacy entry is deleted only when wiping the default home and its key_check matches.
3. A folder whose DB exists but whose key does not verify fails closed with a plain message that names recovery options (passphrase export/backup, `secrets migrate`), and never creates a new key over it.
4. `doctor` warns when a non-default folder is using the legacy entry (existing installs) and offers `secrets migrate --to passphrase` or a per-folder rename.
5. Tests with a fake in-memory keyring (never the real keychain, `FREEMYID_TEST_KEY` unset only inside the fake): two homes -> two entries; wipe of one leaves the other decryptable; legacy default-home path unchanged; the failure in the Goal sequence is reproduced on the old code (strict xfail) and passes on the new.
6. A short recovery note in docs (how to tell if a folder lost its key; what a backup/export restores).
